title: Analysis of Islet Function by Glucagon Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)
author: IIDP-HIPP
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bz9zp976
materials: Preparation of Samples, Standards, and internal Quality Controls
Within 15 minutes of use, combine Color Reagents A and B in equal volume, mix solution thoroughly, and add 200 µL to each well.

Use Prism software to create graphs and to calculate stimulation index (SI) and area under curve (AUC) values. 3.5.1 Stimulation index (SI) is a ratio calculated as maximum response to a given stimulus relative to baseline. 3.5.2 Area under curve (AUC) is calculated by integrating islet secretory response to a given stimulus over time.

steps.title: Thaw archived samples
steps.instruction: Place archived samples in room‑temperature water until thawed, then invert each capped tube ten times to mix.

steps.title: Equilibrate glucagon standard and kit
steps.instruction: Bring the Glucagon Standard to room temperature; store all other kit components at 2–8 °C.

steps.title: Keep hormone extracts on ice
steps.instruction: Retrieve the islet hormone extracts and keep them on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare hormone extract serial dilutions
steps.instruction: In 2 mL tubes, prepare 1:100, 1:1 000, 1:2 000, 1:5 000 and 1:10 000 dilutions of the hormone extract using Calibrator Diluent RD5‑59; vortex each tube before making the next dilution.

steps.title: Prepare glucagon standard dilutions
steps.instruction: Using Calibrator Diluent RD5‑59, make a 1:10 dilution of the 20 000 pg/mL standard vial, then perform six successive 1:2 dilutions; vortex each tube before the next dilution.

steps.title: Reconstitute quality control stocks
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each Quality Control stock in 5 mL distilled water, or thaw existing QC samples if already prepared.

steps.title: Make wash buffer dilution
steps.instruction: Prepare wash buffer by mixing 100 mL buffer concentrate with 900 mL de‑ionized water.

steps.title: Pre‑wash plate wells
steps.instruction: Using the plate washer, add 800 µL diluted wash buffer to each well and soak for 30 seconds, then wash and aspirate the plate twice with 400 µL wash buffer each time.

substeps.instruction: Add 800 µL diluted wash buffer per well; soak 30 s.
Wash and aspirate twice with 400 µL wash buffer.

steps.title: Add assay diluent to wells
steps.instruction: Dispense 150 µL Assay Diluent RD1‑110 into each well.

steps.title: Add standards, controls, and samples
steps.instruction: Using an epMotion 5057 or hand‑pipette, add 50 µL of each standard, control (in duplicate), sample, and extract dilution to the appropriate wells.

steps.title: Incubate with adhesive strip (3 h RT)
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with the supplied adhesive strip and incubate for 3 hours at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate three times
steps.instruction: Using the plate washer, aspirate each well and perform the wash sequence described in step 8; repeat this wash/aspiration cycle three times.

substeps.instruction: Wash with wash buffer as in step 8.
Repeat the entire cycle three times.

steps.title: Add ice‑cold glucagon conjugate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL ice‑cold Glucagon Conjugate to each well.

steps.title: Incubate with adhesive strip (1 h 4 °C)
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with a new adhesive strip and incubate for 1 hour at 4 °C; do not stack plates if running more than one kit.

steps.title: Final wash of plate
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash/aspiration step described in step 12 using the plate washer.

steps.title: Incubate plate (30 min RT, dark)
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 30 minutes at room temperature, protected from light.

steps.title: Add stop solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Stop Solution to each well.

steps.title: Read plate on microplate reader
steps.instruction: Within 30 minutes of adding stop solution, measure optical density at 450 nm with a wavelength correction at 540 nm and calculate glucagon concentrations.

steps.title: Validate standard values
steps.instruction: Confirm that each standard is within ±15 % of its expected value and that duplicate CV ≤20 %; repeat the assay if any standard fails these criteria.

steps.title: Validate quality control values
steps.instruction: Ensure QC samples fall within their known assay ranges; repeat the assay if any QC fails.

steps.title: Calculate average glucagon content
steps.instruction: Average the glucagon concentrations obtained from the four extract dilutions to obtain the glucagon content in pg/mL.

steps.title: Normalize glucagon per islet volume
steps.instruction: Express secreted glucagon as pg/100 IEQs/min and glucagon content as % content/min, normalizing to islet volume (IEQs).
